author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory lists every specialty the clinic knows under its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, on one unpaged page reachable by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: A GET of /specialties.html renders the specialty directory page.
Every specialty the clinic knows is listed under its stored name; no specialty is omitted.
All specialties render on one page: no paging controls and no page parameter.
Each specialty lists the veterinarians holding it, each named first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary").
A veterinarian holding no specialty does not appear anywhere on the page.
A veterinarian holding more than one specialty appears under each of them.
A specialty held by no veterinarian is still listed, shown as held by none.
Specialties, and the veterinarians under each, render in a stable order across repeated requests.
No page of the system gains a navigation entry or link leading to the specialty directory; the existing navigation is unchanged.
Any user-facing wording the page introduces is present in every supported language and none is hard-coded into the page (REQ-LANG-002).
non_goals: Creating, editing, or deleting veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2, confirmed unchanged by the owner).
A navigation entry or any link leading to the specialty directory (NG-10; deferred to a possible follow-up request).
Filtering, searching, or paging the specialty directory.
Any change to the existing veterinarian directory at /vets.html (REQ-VET-001) or to its paging.
notes: Boundary checks. NG-2 is unchanged: the page is read-only, so no scope_overrides are carried; NG-10 is a newly added row. NG-9 declines *searching* for a veterinarian; this page takes no query and lists everything, so NG-9 stands untouched. REQ-SYS-001 still binds: the new page itself carries the existing navigation to owner search and the veterinarian directory — the owner's decision only forbids navigation pointing *at* the new page. Narrowest readings taken where the request was silent: a specialty held by no veterinarian still appears (the request says every specialty the clinic knows); specialty names render as stored, untranslated; a stable presentation order is required but no particular order is fixed. Open question recorded in docs/prd.md (which order to present) rather than raised as a consultation, per the dispatch.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice stays inside the existing vet feature package and adds no module or dependency. Three pieces are new. A SpecialtyRepository follows the PetTypeRepository precedent (Repository pattern, one per persisted root, name-ordered read) — the specialty list cannot come from VetRepository, since a specialty held by no veterinarian is reachable only by reading specialties directly. A SpecialtyDirectory value object groups veterinarians under each specialty; it is the codebase's first derived read model, and it keeps the grouping out of the controller, which architecture-principles.md bars from carrying new rules. A SpecialtyController serves the one route, matching the per-noun controller split the owner package already uses (OwnerController, PetController, VisitController). docs/system-design.md Contracts gained the three rows and one paragraph under 'Invariants the rows cannot carry'. No ADR: every type matches an in-force catalog pattern, so no departure needs recording.
integration_points: SpecialtyController reads specialties through SpecialtyRepository and veterinarians through the existing VetRepository.findAll(), then hands both to SpecialtyDirectory and puts the result in the model.
Vet.specialties is FetchType.EAGER, so the grouping runs safely outside the transaction with spring.jpa.open-in-view disabled.
The new template renders through fragments/layout.html with a menu value no nav item matches; layout.html itself is not edited, which is what keeps NG-10 held.
VetRepository.findAll() is already @Cacheable("vets"); reusing it adds no cache name and leaves CacheConfiguration untouched.

patterns.description: name-ordered lookup repository over a NamedEntity — the shape SpecialtyRepository copies
sorting a NamedEntity collection by name with a Comparator — the ordering idiom to reuse
layout invocation, table markup, and the #{name}/#{specialties}/#{none} keys the new page can reuse verbatim
a controller scoped to one domain noun inside a shared feature package

risks.risk: A new message key added only to messages.properties fails I18nPropertiesSyncTest, which compares base keys against nine locale bundles (messages_en is skipped by fallback).
risks.mitigation: Prefer the existing keys #{specialties}, #{vets}, #{name}, #{none} so the page introduces none. If a heading key is genuinely needed, add it to messages.properties and all nine translated bundles in the same commit. The prd-entry's file_targets name only messages.properties; that is insufficient for a new key.

risks.risk: Adding a menuItem to fragments/layout.html to make the page reachable breaches NG-10 and fails theSiteNavigationShouldNotLeadToTheSpecialtyDirectory.
risks.mitigation: Leave layout.html unchanged. Pass a menu value ('specialties') that matches no nav entry; the fragment then highlights nothing and renders no extra link.

risks.risk: Seeded data holds no specialty without a veterinarian (all three of radiology, surgery, dentistry are held), so the held-by-none case is unobservable against the seed.
risks.mitigation: Cover it in SpecialtyDirectoryTests with real Vet and Specialty instances, and in the controller test through repository doubles. Per CLAUDE.md, prefer hand-written stubs of the two repository interfaces over Mockito; MockMvc remains the sanctioned transport double.

risks.risk: Two veterinarians sharing a full name make an ordering by name alone non-deterministic, which the stable-order criterion needs.
risks.mitigation: Order specialties by name, then veterinarians by last name, first name, and id as final tiebreak. The PRD leaves the particular order open; only stability is required.

risks.risk: SpecialtyDirectory holds references to Vet and Specialty, which are mutable under the persistence-entity exception.
risks.mitigation: Make the directory structurally immutable: static factory, defensive copies, unmodifiable lists, no setters. The referenced entities stay under the granted exception; the new non-entity type is not covered by it and must meet the value-object row in full.

notes: Two adjustments to the prd-entry's file_targets, both design calls the record invites. (1) The route goes on a new SpecialtyController rather than a fourth method on VetController — the codebase splits controllers per domain noun, and VetController stays untouched, so /vets.html carries no regression risk. (2) The specialty query goes on a new SpecialtyRepository rather than VetRepository — the catalog's Repository row is one per aggregate root, and a specialty-returning query on a Vet repository would breach it. Test targets move with them: SpecialtyControllerTests and SpecialtyDirectoryTests rather than additions to VetControllerTests. Open question logged for the product expert, not blocking: docs/ubiquitous-language.md has no entry for 'specialty directory', a term docs/prd.md now uses; that file is the product expert's to write. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit found nothing to judge. Basis for the covering-pattern claims is grep and direct file reads over the vet and owner packages — no IDE oracle is connected in this run, which is the weaker basis.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: SpecialtyDirectory and its nested Entry are the codebase's first non-persisted value objects and are explicitly outside the persistence-entity exception (per the design-block's own risk note: 'the new non-entity type is not covered by it and must meet the value-object row in full'). architecture-principles.md's Value object row requires 'equality by value'. Neither class overrides equals()/hashCode(), so two directories or entries built from the same data compare unequal by reference identity — a trap for the next reader who asserts on a returned SpecialtyDirectory/Entry directly (the existing tests avoid it only by extracting names/lists first) or who reuses either class as a map/set key.
findings.fix: Add value-based equals()/hashCode() to SpecialtyDirectory (over entries) and to Entry (over specialty and veterinarians), or convert both to records if their fields can be exposed as canonical record components without breaking the Javadoc-documented immutability guarantees already in place.

approved_aspects: SpecialtyController, SpecialtyRepository, and SpecialtyDirectory closely mirror the codebase's existing VisitController/PetTypeRepository/Vet.getSpecialties() idioms cited in the design-block, including Javadoc style, defensive copies, and Comparator construction
specialtyList.html reuses the existing #{specialties}/#{name}/#{vets}/#{none} message keys verbatim, avoiding the I18nPropertiesSyncTest risk the design-block flagged
No System.out/err, no swallowed exceptions, no blanket catch, no logging needed in this slice, and checkFormat passes clean
Stable ordering (specialty name, then veterinarian last/first name) is implemented once in SpecialtyDirectory rather than duplicated in the template

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain not verified against the NVD in this review: build.gradle is unchanged (the diff adds no dependency and no repository), the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in this project, and the reviewer has no network access. The resolved Spring Boot 4.1.0 / Jackson set should be closed out by CI or a human against the NVD — this is a standing gap in the project's tooling, not a defect introduced by this change.
approved_aspects: XSS: every user-derived value on src/main/resources/templates/vets/specialtyList.html renders through th:text (escaped by default). No th:utext anywhere in templates, no inline JavaScript, no external resource loading, and no Thymeleaf preprocessing (__${...}__) on any request-derived value — the new page takes no request input at all. Matches the vetList.html precedent line for line (Pattern Consistency).

Injection into data access: SpecialtyRepository.findAll uses a static JPQL @Query with no parameters and no concatenation ('SELECT specialty FROM Specialty specialty ORDER BY specialty.name'); VetRepository.findAll is the existing derived query. No request-derived value reaches any query.

Widening the exposed surface: GET /specialties.html is read-only, takes no path variable, query parameter, or body, and mutates nothing. No management-endpoint exposure changed, no application*.properties touched. The route is no weaker than the documented baseline in docs/system-design.md § Security Context.

Mass assignment: SpecialtyController binds no request data — no @ModelAttribute, no form-backed type, no @InitBinder needed. Nothing new is request-bound, so the identifier-disallow rule has no surface here.

Secrets: no credential, token, key, or connection string in the diff; a case-insensitive sweep for password/secret/token/apikey/credential over the new production, template, and test files returns nothing. No new committed default of any kind.
Path traversal / resource resolution: no filesystem or classpath path is composed anywhere in the change; the view name 'vets/specialtyList' is a compile-time constant.
Deserialization: no Jackson polymorphic typing, no @JsonTypeInfo, no Java serialization, no new PetClinicRuntimeHints entry. The page renders server-side HTML only.

Concurrency: SpecialtyController is a singleton holding only two final repository references. SpecialtyDirectory is built per request and structurally immutable (private constructor, stream .toList() and List.copyOf, no setters), so the shared-mutable-state class is absent. It reads the @Cacheable("vets") collection without mutating it — .stream().sorted() leaves the cached instance untouched, so no request can corrupt the shared cache for later ones.
Error handling and disclosure: no new catch block, no exception message, no logging statement, so nothing new can leak internal detail into the error page that renders exception messages.

Resource allocation: the unpaged full-collection read matches the existing unauthenticated baseline (VetController.java:70 already calls the unpaged vetRepository.findAll()), the result size is bounded by clinic data with no request-controlled multiplier, and no file handle or stream is opened.

Null-safety at the boundary: SpecialtyDirectory.of applies Objects.requireNonNull to both collections and null-safe comparators, so malformed data degrades to an ordering rather than an NPE reaching the error page.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The round-1 fix added equals()/hashCode() to SpecialtyDirectory and Entry (the value-object finding), but the new tests only cover the equal-and-unequal-content cases for SpecialtyDirectory and the equal case for Entry. Jacoco confirms the gap: SpecialtyDirectory.java lines 100 (`this == other` self-equality branch) and 103 (`!(other instanceof SpecialtyDirectory)` type-mismatch/null branch) are both fully uncovered (nc), and the same two branches in Entry.equals (lines 148, 151) are uncovered too. Nothing exercises equals(null), equals(an object of another type), or the reflexive `x.equals(x)` case for either class, and Entry has no not-equal counterpart to the Directory-level theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldNotEqualADirectoryOverAnotherSpecialty test. A future edit that breaks null-safety or drops the reflexive shortcut in either equals() would pass every test in this file.
findings.fix: Add, for both SpecialtyDirectory and Entry: a self-equality assertion (assertThat(x).isEqualTo(x)), an assertThat(x).isNotEqualTo(null), an assertThat(x).isNotEqualTo(anUnrelatedObject) (e.g. a String), and — mirroring the existing Directory-level negative test — an Entry-level not-equal case (e.g. same specialty, different veterinarians, or a different specialty).

approved_aspects: Round-1 finding on SpecialtyDirectory/Entry value-object equality is otherwise well covered: equal-content, order-independence of specialty input (built in reverse order), and unequal-specialty cases are all tested with AssertJ's isEqualTo/isNotEqualTo/hasSameHashCodeAs

All prior review-round approvals still hold: real hand-written repository stubs (no Mockito), BDD naming, three-tier data naming, four-phase test structure, and full PRD acceptance-criteria coverage are unchanged by the fix delta

./gradlew test passes with no failures or skips across the full suite; SpecialtyDirectory instruction coverage is 96% and Entry 93%, both above the brief's 80% line-coverage target even with the branch gap noted above
